beliefs.practice: Do not commit the DocumentDB connection string or primary key to source control; read DOCUMENTDB_URI (and any keys) from environment variables or a secrets store at runtime.
Prefer using a secrets manager (Azure Key Vault) or managed identity to store and retrieve the cluster credentials instead of raw env vars when running in cloud or CI/CD.
Always connect with TLS/SSL enforced (e.g., mongodb+srv or tls=true in the connection string) and verify server certificates; disallow insecure connections in production.

Configure connection pooling and timeouts in the MongoDB driver (set reasonable maxPoolSize, connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS, serverSelectionTimeoutMS) to avoid exhausting sockets and to ensure fast failover.
Enable and implement exponential backoff with jitter for retrying transient network and server selection errors, and make retries idempotent-aware (do not retry non-idempotent writes blindly).
Set appropriate write concern and read concern for your risk-review workload (e.g., majority or w=1 depending on durability vs latency needs) and document this in configuration.
Use a dedicated database name (sample_banking_11) and limit the application's actions to that database only (do not list or modify other databases), and validate the app uses that configured DB.

Model correspondent and source documents with a stable unique _id, include metadata fields (source, created_at, updated_at, text_snippet, embedding_dim), and keep document sizes well below the DB's max document size (avoid >16MB).

Store embeddings as a fixed-length numeric array field and record the embedding dimension in the document; ensure all stored embeddings across collections have identical dimensionality to the index configuration.

When creating the server-side vector index, explicitly set the index type (HNSW, IVF, DiskANN) and metric (cosine or euclidean/L2) to match the embedding model and tune parameters (efConstruction, M, nlist, etc.) for the dataset size and latency needs.

Create additional non-vector indexes on frequently queried fields (e.g., bank_id, sanction_list_id, last_reviewed, risk_score) and use compound or partial indexes where appropriate to speed metadata filtering before vector search.
Use projection to return only required fields (avoid returning full text and embeddings when not needed) to reduce network transfer and memory pressure in review API responses.

When server-side vector search is not available or limited, provide a documented, auditable fallback (e.g., local FAISS/Annoy search using seeded or synthetic embeddings) and flag results as coming from fallback logic.
Normalize embeddings consistently (unit-normalize for cosine similarity or leave raw for L2) before storage and before query-time embedding generation so distance metrics behave predictably.
Limit and paginate search results (e.g., topK + offset or cursor) and enforce a max result size in the /review API to avoid expensive large scans and to make risk narratives deterministic.

Use deterministic and auditable scoring: store match metadata (matched_ids, distances, match_text_snippets, timestamp) with each review run so risk scores and narratives can be reproduced and audited later.
Avoid expensive multi-document transactions for high-throughput vector inserts; batch writes and use ordered=false with retries for bulk seeding, and verify idempotency of seed scripts.
When seeding sample data, mark it with an identifiable field (e.g., seeded=true and seed_version) so test data can be filtered or removed without affecting production records.

Implement monitoring and alerting on connection errors, slow queries, vector index health, and RU/throughput or CPU/memory metrics; enable driver command monitoring or Azure diagnostic logs as available.
Harden network access: restrict the cluster to known client IPs, use VNet private endpoints if available, and avoid exposing the DB's primary key to browsers or client-side code.

Use schema validation (collection validators) or application-level validation for critical fields (embedding array length, required metadata, date format) and fail fast on malformed documents during seed or ingestion.

For high-cardinality or growing datasets, choose an appropriate shard key (or partition key) based on query patterns (e.g., hash(bank_id) or reviewed_date) and test distribution to avoid hot partitions.
Avoid storing raw PII in searchable fields; redact or tokenise sensitive fields in sanctions/adverse-media documents and store provenance metadata to preserve utility while reducing exposure.
Index maintenance: when changing vector index parameters or reindexing, perform it during a maintenance window and re-seed a small subset first to measure impact on latency and storage.
Make the review operation idempotent and safe to rerun: persist review run identifiers, last_processed timestamps, and incremental cursors to support retries and resumable runs.
